leads.summary: Toggle can close an unrelated focused window when its title mentions the target app-id, or its class matches the unescaped regex.
leads.consequence: With `--toggle btop`, a focused Firefox window titled `Guide to org.omarchy.btop` is dispatched to close at its address instead of focusing/launching btop. Even `orgXomarchyYbtop` matches the dots in the pattern. This reuses an existing broad focus predicate but changes the consequence from focus to close. A future merge with open #9927 would exclude org.quickshell in the shared helper, but the new active-window check does not inherit that exclusion. Command exits 0; another click repeats the action unless that window is gone. Prefer checking the actual TUI class/app-id before destructive close, or explicitly restrict title fallback to known terminal identity.
leads.triage: corroborates Opus F4; regex-dot wildcard detail is standard jq regex semantics, added to F4 note

leads.summary: An empty --app-id turns the new close predicate into a match-anything selector; --toggle without a command can also close an unintended TUI.
leads.consequence: `--toggle --app-id= btop` sets APP_ID to the empty string, so `test(\b\b)` matches a word boundary in an unrelated active Firefox window; the script closes Firefox and returns 0. `--toggle` without any command derives `org.omarchy.` and its trailing dot plus word boundary can match the prefix of a TUI app class (sandbox: btop address 0x44), again closes without a valid target. Reject empty --app-id and missing command before querying or dispatching; the CLI's metadata only displays required args and does not enforce them when --toggle was supplied.
leads.triage: empty --app-id= corroborates Opus F4 (published). '--toggle with no command' variant not independently confirmed; dropped

leads.summary: Failed close operations are reported as success, and a real Hyprland warning suppresses the fallback entirely.
leads.consequence: If both hyprctl dispatches fail nonzero, the script still exits 0 after printing only fallback stderr. More subtly, Hyprland 0.56.2's `noclosefor` can reject `hl.dsp.window.close` with a `warning:` result while hyprctl exits 0; the Lua output is redirected away, the `||` fallback is skipped, and toggle silently leaves the window open while reporting success. The next click repeats. Preserve/report the dispatch result and inspect warnings if treating status zero as confirmation; do not force-close windows subject to noclosefor.
leads.triage: corroborates Opus F2; noclosefor warning/exit-0 path also in Opus report (confirmed working notes); not separately published

leads.summary: The shipped custom bar widget example still calls the launcher without --toggle.
leads.consequence: A user who follows the project's only sample for an onClicked TUI bar widget gets the old launch/focus behavior, not the new click-to-close behavior; this PR changes no caller to pass --toggle, so the added mode remains opt-in and undiscoverable in the relevant example. Change the sample action to `omarchy-launch-or-focus-tui --toggle btop` (or add a separate toggle example), and describe how it differs from the existing non-toggle action. Factual source observation, not a runtime reproduction.
leads.triage: factual, verified shell/plugins/bar/README.md:149 has no --toggle; judged low value, not published

leads.summary: No shipped test exercises the new close branch or its error handling, while adjacent focus and close dispatchers have tests.
leads.consequence: A plausible mutant that always leaves TOGGLE=0, or exits 0 after both dispatches fail, satisfies the existing metadata/style tests and the sibling close-all test, since none runs the changed script with `--toggle`. The separate sandbox regression fixtures above fail on wrong-window, empty-id, and close-failure paths. ## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Outcome:** With default focus-follows-mouse, the btop close is likely unreachable when a tiled window sits between it and the bar.

### Close is hard to reach with focus-follows-mouse

With `follow_mouse = 1` and btop floating, crossing a tiled window from btop to the bar focuses that window, so the click refocuses btop and warps the pointer back into it. **Impact:** it closes only if the pointer reaches the bar without crossing another window. From Hyprland 0.56.2 source; not reproduced.

**Suggested change:** treat the TUI as open when it is on the active workspace, not only when focused, or document this.

### A failed close exits 0

If both dispatch forms fail, the fallback prints its error and `exit 0` still runs. **Impact:** the exit status hides the failed close.

**Suggested change:** use `if`/`else` with the dispatch last in its branch (fallback to `/dev/null`), per the AGENTS.md rule on `exit`.

# Reproducer: toggle-exit-status

Reviewed head: omacom/omarchy `436aa60629e3c53e387f871b5a32cc7de2eb41ae` (PR #13499).

**Claim:** When both close dispatches fail, `--toggle` still exits 0 (the fallback's error text is printed, then `exit 0`).

The stub `hyprctl` answers every `dispatch` with `error: close failed` and exit status 7, which is how `hyprctl` 0.56.x reports a reply starting with `error:`. The test expects a nonzero exit status.

Save as `test/shell.d/launch-or-focus-tui-toggle-exit-test.sh` in a checkout of the PR head and run `bash test/shell.d/launch-or-focus-tui-toggle-exit-test.sh`. All commands are stubs; nothing talks to a compositor.

```bash
#!/bin/bash

set -euo pipefail

source "$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)/base-test.sh"

test_tmp=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$test_tmp"' EXIT

mock_bin="$test_tmp/bin"
call_log="$test_tmp/calls.log"
mkdir -p "$mock_bin"

# Both close forms fail, the way hyprctl reports an "error:" reply (exit 7).
cat >"$mock_bin/hyprctl" <<'SH'
#!/bin/bash
printf 'hyprctl %s\n' "$*" >>"$CALL_LOG"
case $1 in
  activewindow) printf '%s\n' '{"address":"0xb7","class":"org.omarchy.btop","title":"btop"}' ;;
  dispatch) echo "error: close failed"; exit 7 ;;
esac
SH
chmod +x "$mock_bin/hyprctl"

status=0
PATH="$mock_bin:$ROOT/bin:$PATH" CALL_LOG="$call_log" \
  bash "$ROOT/bin/omarchy-launch-or-focus-tui" --toggle btop >"$test_tmp/stdout" 2>&1 || status=$?

grep -Fq 'closewindow address:0xb7' "$call_log" || fail "toggle tries the classic close form after the Lua form fails" "$(cat "$call_log")"
(( status != 0 )) || fail "toggle reports a close that failed in both forms" "exit status: $status; output: $(cat "$test_tmp/stdout")"
pass "toggle reports a close that failed in both forms"
```

Actual output at the reviewed head (exit status 1):

```text
exit status: 0; output: error: close failed
not ok - toggle reports a close that failed in both forms
```

<details><summary>More findings</summary>

### `--app-id` before `--toggle` launches `--toggle` as the command

Only a leading `--toggle` is recognised, so `--app-id=org.omarchy.btop --toggle btop` runs `xdg-terminal-exec ... -e --toggle btop` when btop is not open. **Impact:** a wrong launch for that argument order (the documented order is `[--toggle] [--app-id=<app-id>]`).

**Suggested change:** also accept `--toggle` right after `--app-id=`, or reject that order with a usage message.

# Reproducer: app-id-before-toggle

Reviewed head: omacom/omarchy `436aa60629e3c53e387f871b5a32cc7de2eb41ae` (PR #13499).

**Claim:** `--app-id=... --toggle <command>` does not toggle; `--toggle` is passed on to the terminal as the command to run.

Only `--toggle` as the first argument is recognised. With `--app-id` first, the launch path runs `xdg-terminal-exec ... -e --toggle btop`. The stub `uwsm-app` logs the terminal command line instead of starting anything.

Save as `test/shell.d/launch-or-focus-tui-toggle-order-test.sh` in a checkout of the PR head and run `bash test/shell.d/launch-or-focus-tui-toggle-order-test.sh`. All commands are stubs; nothing talks to a compositor.

```bash
#!/bin/bash

set -euo pipefail

source "$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)/base-test.sh"

test_tmp=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$test_tmp"' EXIT

mock_bin="$test_tmp/bin"
call_log="$test_tmp/calls.log"

cat >"$mock_bin/hyprctl" <<'SH'

case $1 in
  activewindow) printf '%s\n' '{"address":"0xf1","class":"firefox","title":"Mozilla Firefox"}' ;;
  clients) printf '%s\n' '[{"address":"0xf1","class":"firefox","title":"Mozilla Firefox"}]' ;;

esac

# Follow the launch chain as far as the terminal command line.
cat >"$mock_bin/setsid" <<'SH'

SH
cat >"$mock_bin/uwsm-app" <<'SH'

SH
```

Actual output at the reviewed head (exit status 1):

```text
hyprctl clients -j
uwsm-app -- xdg-terminal-exec --app-id=org.omarchy.btop -e --toggle btop
not ok - --toggle after --app-id is not handed to the terminal as the command
```

### The close can hit an unrelated focused window

The match is copied from `omarchy-launch-or-focus`, where an over-match only focuses the wrong window. With `--toggle` it sends a close instead: a focused window whose title contains the id (the `.` characters in the id are regex wildcards), or any focused window when `--app-id=` is empty (pattern `\b\b`). **Impact:** low likelihood with the default `org.omarchy.<command>` ids, but the close request goes to the wrong window.

**Suggested change:** in the close branch, match the class only and skip the close when the id is empty.

<details><summary>Details</summary>

**Verified** (stub `hyprctl` sandbox tests, plus `git merge-file` for the last item):
- `--toggle btop` with btop focused dispatches `hl.dsp.window.close({ window = "address:..." })` and exits 0; with btop open elsewhere it focuses it; with btop not open it launches `omarchy-launch-tui btop` without `--toggle`.
- `activewindow` returning `{}` (no focused window) falls through to the focus path.
- Calls without `--toggle` give the same calls, output and exit status as the merge base.
- `omarchy commands --check` passes and help shows the new `[--toggle]` argument.
- #13674, #12800 and #9490 each merge with this PR without conflict markers in `bin/omarchy-launch-or-focus-tui`.

**Optional notes:**
- The `closewindow address:` fallback cannot help on a Lua config: Hyprland evaluates every `hyprctl dispatch <x>` as `hl.dispatch(<x>)`, so the string form is always a Lua syntax error there, by design rather than on "some builds". Also, `omarchy-hyprland-window-close-all` uses only the Lua form for close. The code comment could say so, or the fallback could be dropped.
- **Optional test improvement:** the script has no test. A five-check `test/shell.d` stub test (close, focus, launch, no focused window, non-toggle) passes at the head and fails at the merge base, so it would catch a toggle branch that stops working.
</details>
